tour.title: Application Shell: Root Layout
tour.description: The entry point of the web app. RootLayout configures Google Fonts (Geist, JetBrains Mono), imports global CSS from the shared UI package, and wraps all pages in a ThemeProvider and TooltipProvider. Notice how it already demonstrates the monorepo import pattern: UI components and utilities come from @workspace/ui.

tour.title: Theme & Provider Layer
tour.description: The ThemeProvider is a client component that wraps next-themes to provide dark/light mode switching with a class-based strategy. It also registers a keyboard shortcut (press 'd' to toggle themes) via the ThemeHotkey sub-component. This is the first layer of context that every page inherits.

tour.title: Pages: Where Features Live
tour.description: The home page and test page show how app routes consume shared UI components via the @workspace/ui import path. Even a minimal page like page.tsx imports Button from the shared package, demonstrating that all UI primitives live in packages/ui, not in the app itself.

tour.title: Shared UI: The cn() Utility Foundation
tour.description: Every UI component in the project depends on cn(), a tiny function that merges Tailwind CSS classes using clsx and tailwind-merge. This utility prevents class conflicts and is the single most-imported module across the entire packages/ui directory.

tour.title: Component Design: Button as Blueprint
tour.description: The Button component demonstrates the standard pattern used across all 56 shadcn components: class-variance-authority (cva) defines typed variant props, cn() merges them with user classes, and a Base UI primitive handles accessibility. Every component in packages/ui follows this same structure.

tour.title: Complex UI: Sidebar Context Provider
tour.description: The Sidebar is the most complex component at 726 lines. It uses the React Context provider pattern to share state (expanded/collapsed, mobile/desktop) across deeply nested sub-components. It also composes several simpler UI primitives (Sheet, Tooltip, Skeleton, Button) showing how the component library layers together.

tour.title: Database Schema: Star-Schema Design
tour.description: The data model follows a star-schema pattern. Three dimension tables (artists, albums, tracks) describe music entities with MusicBrainz IDs and foreign-key relationships, while one fact table (scrobbles) records each listen event with a timestamp and source. Shared column definitions like timestampsWithoutUpdate keep the schema DRY.

tour.title: Database Client & Configuration
tour.description: The db package exports a Drizzle ORM client connected to Neon Postgres via their serverless HTTP driver. The createDb factory accepts a URL so both the web app and import scripts can create their own connections. Drizzle Kit config points at the schema files and filters to the 'listen' Postgres schema.

tour.title: Data Pipeline: LastFM Import
tour.description: The import app is a standalone script that fetches recent scrobbles from the LastFM API and upserts them into the star-schema tables. Each track is resolved through a chain of upsertArtist, upsertAlbum, upsertTrack calls that handle race conditions with onConflictDoNothing plus re-query. This is the primary data ingestion pathway for the platform.

tour.title: Tooling & Automation
tour.description: The ESLint config package provides shared linting rules (TypeScript, Prettier, Turbo) that all workspace packages extend, keeping code style consistent across the monorepo. ralph.sh is the automation harness: a bash loop that invokes the Claude CLI up to N iterations, checking for a completion signal, enabling autonomous multi-step development workflows.
